title: Model match · Level 2: The arm's step
brief: Predict a step of the arm bench's motor on port 3 (an EV3 Large through a 12:36 gear to a 150 mm arm with a 100 g tip, hanging at rest), from rest. The course sets line 1 to `d = <duty>`, drawn 40 to 80 % per run. Before the step, write your model's 151 predictions of Motor(3).speed() / 3 (the arm's deg/s: Motor(3) is the motor, ungeared) in deg/s, for t = 0, 0.002, ..., 0.3 s, to the flash file predict.txt (numbers separated by blanks, commas or new lines); then call Motor(3).dc(d) and hold it, the program still running (a wait past the window): the run ends 0.3 s after the step. The course reads Motor(3).speed() / 3 (the arm's deg/s: Motor(3) is the motor, ungeared) every 2 ms from the step (t = 0 is the reading before the duty acts) to 0.3 s, both included. NRMSE = rms(prediction - reading) / y_ss, y_ss the reading at the window's end; a run scores 100 x clamp(1 - NRMSE / 0.15, 0, 1), and 0 when the step is not dc(d) held to the end, when a built-in move ran on port 3, or when any other motor (ports 1, 2, 4) drew energy. Ten runs; pass: a mean of 60 or more and 8 runs predicted. The window ends before the arm passes horizontal. Practice until COURSE and LAB ship. Par: the reference model's mean score on seed 0, 99.0 (mean NRMSE 0.14 %).

score.run: if(predicted & stepped & stepHeld & stepDuty == d & moveTicks == 0 & energy_1 == 0 & energy_2 == 0 & energy_4 == 0, 100 * clamp(1 - nrmse / 0.15, 0, 1), 0)
